name: repair-priority
description: Grade one failing all-pages gate row (0.26.0) on what a reader would suffer, so code can order the repair queue and decide what ships with a documented residual. Composite-scoring shape: three independent scores, weights live in the caller (#127).

fields.row: { path, template, tier, pixelPct, textPct, heightDelta, clipped: {textClipped, textHidden, controlHidden, controlClipped}, content: {missing, hidden, examples: [text of up to 8 missing/hidden links and headings]}, reasons }

instructions.question: How badly would a reader of the build page in `row` be affected by the recorded failures?
instructions.focus: Judge from the failing criteria and the named elements; a pixel percentage alone with nothing missing, clipped or hidden is cosmetic.

criteria.summary: Cosmetic: geometry or colour differs, nothing missing, clipped or hidden; every link and heading present.
signals: pixel over the bar with clipped 0 and content 0

criteria.summary: Degraded: some text is clipped or a control is partly cut, but the page's purpose and every path through it remain usable.
Broken in part: a section a reader came for is unusable — cards with clipped descriptions and hidden detail links, a hidden primary CTA, missing headings that structure the page.
signals: hidden links in a repeated unit

criteria.summary: Unusable: the page's main content or navigation is missing or hidden, or the render is thousands of pixels off.
signals: height delta a large share of the page

instructions.question: How much of the page in `row` do the failures touch?

criteria.summary: One element or one small band.
One section or one repeated unit type.
Most of the page or every repeated unit.

template_wide.instructions: Do the failures in `row` look like a property of the page's template or shared block (every unit affected the same way, chrome geometry, a shared container) rather than of this page's own content?

criteria.true: Every repeated unit fails the same way, or the failing element is chrome or a shared container: fixing the block fixes every page of the template.
criteria.false: The failure is tied to this page's particular content or a one-off element.
